statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low), with no Nasdaq-100 price path available during the CME weekend halt.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the two hours after it (00:00-03:00 Berlin on 5 October), where the forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a record close through the weekend futures halt, with an unattributed Aramco fire and a reported Saudi offensive framing the Sunday reopen
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor. The last observed path was orderly: the index traded to an all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, fully retraced it, and finished at a record 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the session range, up 1.00%, with VIX settling at 15.31, down 6.59%. A fully retraced record high is two-way behaviour rather than the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure Tail measures.

Stress is high rather than low because the backdrop behind that record close is unusually tense. Brent settled near 102.6 after a 2.6% decline, and the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%. The Saudi-Houthi conflict escalated further over the weekend: the Houthis claimed a ballistic-missile and drone strike on an Aramco facility south of Riyadh on 3 October, witnesses and news agencies reported flames and smoke at the site, and the Saudi-led coalition spokesman called the Houthi account misleading. Neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco have confirmed the cause of the fire, any damage, or any impact on production, refining or exports. Yemeni government forces reported 97 targeting operations against Houthi positions, and reporting published on 2 October describes Riyadh preparing an offensive of more than 100,000 Yemeni troops, supported by Saudi air strikes, to reverse Houthi control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait within weeks. Saudi-linked tanker war-risk premiums at Yanbu have tripled to roughly 3% of vessel value since early July.

None of that is observed Nasdaq-100 structure. Event importance, supply-risk headlines and elevated oil raise Stress and shape Confidence; they do not mechanically raise Tail. Confidence of 84% reflects complete verified coverage of levels, yields, oil, volatility, geopolitics and the seven-day calendar against the complete absence of a live price path. The published danger window spans the 22:00Z reopen and the two hours after it, where forecast Tail reaches the WATCH band on gap and thin-liquidity discontinuity risk. That forecast decays on the assumption that reopen discovery is orderly; NQ holding a session extreme with shallow or failed retracements would invalidate it. The week's first high-impact scheduled checkpoint is ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October, followed by FOMC minutes at 18:00Z on 7 October.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours Claude published Tail between 7% and 3%, reaching a 3% floor from 12:00Z on 3 October and holding there through the weekend halt, while Stress fell to 52% in the European afternoon and then rebuilt steadily to 76% by 06:00Z. Confidence stayed in the 83-88% band. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode was normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The closed Sunday session carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held at 3-6% through 20:00Z while Stress rebuilds from 77% to a 79% ceiling as unpriced weekend headline flow accumulates. Tail then steps to 12% in the final closed hour and is raised to 21-23%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the two hours after it, which form the published danger window. It decays conditionally to 10% by 06:00Z on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, an assumption that NQ holding a session extreme without meaningful retracement would invalidate. Confidence troughs at 79% in the final closed hour and recovers to 85% once a continuous path is observable again.

forecastDetail.comment: No Nasdaq-100 price path exists during the CME weekend halt, so Tail holds its 3% floor while the last observed session, a fully retraced record high into a lower-quarter close, remains two-way rather than pathological.
A second closed hour with no scoreable structure; Stress stays high because the cause of the Riyadh Aramco fire and any damage to refining or exports remain officially unconfirmed.
Confidence eases as the evidence set stops refreshing during the halt, while Brent near 102.6 and a 5.24% 10-year keep the Stress floor elevated rather than low.
Reported preparation of a large Saudi-backed offensive to retake Bab el-Mandeb is a structural supply risk that lifts Stress slightly; it is not an observed Nasdaq-100 path and does not move Tail.
Tail is nudged to 4% only because unpriced headline exposure accumulates toward the 22:00Z reopen; no structure has been observed in this hour.
Tripled Yanbu tanker war-risk premiums are a verified cost signal supporting high Stress, while Tail stays at the floor in the absence of any live price path.
